questions.text: The number of possible min-heaps containing each value from {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7} exactly once is _____.
questions.solution:
The root must be 1. The 6 remaining numbers split into the left and right subtrees (3 each): [latex]\binom63=20[/latex] ways. In each 3-node subtree the smallest is its root and the other two can be swapped: 2 ways each.

Total = 20 [latex]\times[/latex] 2 [latex]\times[/latex] 2 = 80

Answer: 80

questions.text: The postorder traversal of a binary tree is 8,9,6,7,4,5,2,3,1. The inorder traversal of the same tree is 8,6,9,4,7,2,5,1,3. The height of a tree is the length of the longest path from the root to any leaf. The height of the binary tree above is ______.
questions.solution:
Postorder ends with 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] root 1. Inorder splits into left {8, 6, 9, 4, 7, 2, 5} and right {3}.
- Left subtree: root 2 (last in its postorder), with left {8, 6, 9, 4, 7} and right {5}.
- {8, 6, 9, 4, 7}: root 4, left {8, 6, 9} (root 6 with children 8, 9), right {7}.

Longest path: 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 4 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 6 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 8 = 4 edges.

Answer: 4

questions.text:
A queue is implemented using a non-circular singly linked list. The queue has a head pointer and a tail pointer, as shown in the figure. Let n denote the number of nodes in the queue. Let enqueue be implemented by inserting a new node at the head, and dequeue be implemented by deletion of a node from the tail.

Which one of the following is the time complexity of the most time-efficient implementation of enqueue and dequeue, respectively, for this data structure?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Enqueue at the head: create a node and point it to the old head [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]\Theta(1)[/latex].
- Dequeue at the tail: removing the tail needs the node before it, and in a singly linked list that means walking from the head [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]\Theta(n)[/latex].

Answer: [latex]\Theta(1),\Theta(n)[/latex]

questions.text:
Choose the equivalent prefix form of the following expression
[latex](a+(b-c))^{\star}((d-e) /(f+g-h))[/latex]
questions.solution:
Convert each part to prefix:
- a + (b [latex]-[/latex] c) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] + a [latex]-[/latex] b c
- (d [latex]-[/latex] e) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]-[/latex] d e; (f + g [latex]-[/latex] h) = ((f + g) [latex]-[/latex] h) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]-[/latex] + f g h
- (d [latex]-[/latex] e) / (f + g [latex]-[/latex] h) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] / [latex]-[/latex] d e [latex]-[/latex] + f g h

Whole: * + a [latex]-[/latex] b c / [latex]-[/latex] d e [latex]-[/latex] + f g h

Answer: Option 1

questions.text: The best data structure to check whether an arithmetic expression has  balanced parenthesis is  a:
questions.solution:
Push each opening bracket and pop when the matching closing bracket appears. The expression is balanced if the stack is empty at the end and no pop fails.

Answer: Stack
